Such conferences are typically used by management to discuss strategic initiatives, operational updates, and the company's current market position.

items.title: RBC Capital and Seaport Initiate Coverage of Tesla
items.summary: Analysts at RBC Capital and Seaport have initiated coverage of Tesla, both assigning the stock a 'Buy' rating.
items.content: RBC Capital analyst Kenneth Herbert initiated coverage of Tesla with a 'Buy' rating and a price target of $480. Separately, Seaport analyst Ron Jewsikow also initiated coverage with a 'Buy' rating, citing the company's robotaxi business as a significant long-term opportunity. Jewsikow noted that Tesla's progress in the robotaxi space has become difficult to ignore, projecting potential for substantial market value growth by 2040. These initiations reflect renewed analyst interest in the company's autonomous driving and ride-hailing strategy.

items.title: Boeing Awarded $2.82 Billion Air Force Contract Modification
items.summary: The U.S. Air Force has awarded Boeing a $2.82 billion contract modification for the production of 15 KC-46A Lot 13 aircraft, along with associated subscriptions and licenses.
items.content: Boeing received a $2.82 billion contract modification from the U.S. Air Force to support the production of 15 KC-46A Lot 13 aircraft. The agreement also includes provisions for subscriptions and licenses related to the program. Work on this contract is scheduled to be performed in Seattle and is expected to reach completion by June 30, 2030.

items.title: Marriott Bonvoy Recognized in 2027 BrandSpark Most Trusted® Awards
items.summary: Marriott Bonvoy has been named the most trusted hotel loyalty program in Canada as part of the 2027 BrandSpark Most Trusted® Awards.
items.content: Marriott Bonvoy received recognition as the top-ranked brand in the hotel loyalty program category in the 2027 edition of the BrandSpark Most Trusted® Awards. The awards are determined by Canadian consumer feedback across 324 distinct categories. This recognition highlights the brand's standing among Canadian shoppers.

items.title: Class Action Lawsuit Filed Against Uber Regarding October 2026 Data Breach
items.summary: A proposed class action lawsuit alleges that Uber Technologies and Fireworks.AI failed to adequately protect sensitive driver information during an October 2026 data breach.
items.content: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Uber Technologies, Inc. and artificial intelligence provider Fireworks.AI, alleging negligence in safeguarding sensitive driver data. The complaint claims that an unauthorized third party accessed Uber's systems through compromised Fireworks.AI credentials, exposing information such as driver's license images, names, addresses, and dates of birth. The lawsuit, filed in November 2026, further alleges that Uber failed to provide timely notification to impacted individuals, waiting approximately one month after the breach was discovered on October 9. Plaintiffs argue that this delay and the company's cybersecurity measures have increased the risk of identity theft and fraud for affected drivers.

items.title: Micware Co., Ltd. Announces Participation in Upcoming Investor Events
items.summary: Micware Co., Ltd. announced that its Co-Founder and Chief Financial Officer, Mr. Takuma Segawa, will participate in three investor events in December 2026.
items.content: Micware Co., Ltd. announced that Co-Founder and CFO Takuma Segawa, along with the company's Investor Relations team, will participate in a series of investor engagements in December 2026. The schedule includes Non-Deal Roadshows in Boston on December 8 and in New York on December 9 and 11, hosted by Alphaterra Advisory. Additionally, Mr. Segawa will attend the StoneX 15th Annual Discovery One-on-One Investor Conference in New York on December 10 and participate in the Emerging Growth Virtual Conference on the same day. These events will involve one-on-one and group meetings with institutional investors to discuss the company's business and strategy.

items.title: Micron Discloses Increased Executive Security Expenses
items.summary: Micron Technology's latest proxy filing reveals a significant increase in security spending for CEO Sanjay Mehrotra.
items.content: In a proxy filing disclosed on November 24, 2026, Micron Technology reported that it spent $764,748 on executive security for CEO Sanjay Mehrotra during the fiscal year ending in August. This figure represents an approximately 2,000% increase from the $35,636 spent on personal security arrangements in the prior fiscal year. The company stated that the increased costs were implemented to provide more comprehensive security in light of a heightened external threat environment. The filing also disclosed security expenditures for other executives, including $75,175 for Chief Business Officer Sumit Sadana.

items.title: BlackRock Canada Announces November 2026 Cash Distributions for iShares Premium Money Market ETF
items.summary: BlackRock Asset Management Canada Limited, a subsidiary of BlackRock, Inc., announced the final cash distributions for the iShares Premium Money Market ETF for November 2026.
items.content: BlackRock Asset Management Canada Limited, an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of BlackRock, Inc., has declared the final cash distributions for the iShares Premium Money Market ETF for November 2026. Unitholders of record as of November 25, 2026, are eligible to receive the distributions, which are payable on November 30, 2026. The announcement provides details regarding the final per-unit distribution amounts for the fund.

items.title: Juries Award Millions in Separate Johnson & Johnson Talc-Related Mesothelioma Lawsuits
items.summary: Two separate juries in Massachusetts and California awarded millions of dollars in damages in lawsuits alleging that Johnson & Johnson's talc-based baby powder caused mesothelioma.
items.content: On November 24, 2026, juries in Massachusetts and California returned verdicts against Johnson & Johnson in separate mesothelioma cases involving the company's talc-based baby powder. A Suffolk County Superior Court jury in Massachusetts awarded approximately $3.3 million, including court-ordered interest, to the family of a plaintiff who developed mesothelioma after years of product use. Separately, a Northern California jury awarded $34.21 million to a plaintiff who also developed mesothelioma after decades of using the company's talc products. In both instances, jurors determined that the company failed to provide adequate warnings regarding the risk of asbestos contamination in its products, which they found to be a substantial factor in the plaintiffs' diagnoses.

GCG Advisory Partners' Bill Gunderson makes the case that Nvidia is the cheapest growth stock in the market at nine times forward earnings and names Nvidia and Eli Lilly as his top picks for 2027. Brian breaks down Dell's blowout quarter and $132 billion AI backlog, and HPE CEO Antonio Neri joins to explain the company's raised outlook, why it refuses to finance neoclouds, and whether server margins have peaked. Brian closes by arguing the AI trade is reaching consumers' wallets, pointing to Best Buy's strongest comparable sales growth in five years.

items.title: Best Buy also among companies benefiting from AI boom
